resources.string: No ads. Nothing leaves your phone.
Fading · will pause whatever is playing
Couldn\'t pause; muted instead. Tap Restore volume, or it comes back by itself at %1$s if nothing is playing then.
Notifications are off. The timer will still run, but you won\'t see the countdown or controls.
In the last 5 minutes and during the fade, shake the phone twice to add %1$d min. The phone buzzes once to confirm. Keeps the processor awake for those minutes only.
No ads, no network. Media is paused with the media button and audio focus. Special access only if you turn on a feature that needs it:
Accessibility: locks the screen (and goes Home) when a timer ends, and draws the Goodnight dark layer. Reads nothing on your screen.
Notification access: pauses playing media directly. Never reads your notifications.
Modify system settings: sets the screen timeout to 15 s after the pause, and (Goodnight without accessibility) lowers the brightness; puts yours back once the screen is off.
Turn any of them off in Android Settings, or with the switch here.
Start a preset, see the countdown, extend or stop without opening the app.
After the pause, turns the screen off and locks it, like pressing the power button.
Needs Android 9 or newer. Use Turn screen off sooner instead.
Leaves the video app before locking, so it can\'t start playing again when you unlock.
Used when locking is off or not available: sets the screen timeout to 15 s after the pause and puts yours back once the screen is off.
For players that ignore the normal pause: pauses every playing app directly before trying the usual way.
Turned off: accessibility access for Sleep Timer is off. Turn screen off sooner still works without it.
Turned off: notification access for Sleep Timer is off. The normal pause is used.
Turned off: Modify system settings is not allowed for Sleep Timer.
Not turned on: accessibility access was not allowed.
Not turned on: notification access was not allowed.
Not turned on: Modify system settings was not allowed.

Sleep Timer uses Android's accessibility service only to lock the screen when a timer ends and, if you turn it on, to go to the Home screen first. If you turn on Goodnight, it also uses it to draw a dark (optionally warm) layer over the screen and to lower the screen brightness through that layer.

It reads nothing on your screen, sees nothing you type, and sends nothing anywhere. The app has no internet access.

The screen is locked the same way the power button locks it, so your usual unlock (fingerprint, face, PIN) stays the same.

Next: Android opens Accessibility settings. Tap Sleep Timer Trial there and turn it on. You can turn it off there at any time.
If the switch there is greyed out (app installed from a file), open App info for Sleep Timer Trial, tap ⋮, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.

Some players ignore the normal pause. With notification access, Sleep Timer can see which apps are playing and pause them directly when a timer ends.

Android calls this Notification access, but Sleep Timer never reads, stores or reacts to your notifications. It only looks at whether each media player is playing, and sends nothing anywhere.

Next: Android opens the Notification access page. Allow it for Sleep Timer Trial. You can turn it off there at any time.
If the switch there is greyed out (app installed from a file), open App info for Sleep Timer Trial, tap ⋮, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.

When a timer ends, Sleep Timer sets your screen timeout to 15 seconds, so the screen turns off soon after the pause. As soon as the screen is off, your own timeout is put back. If you change the timeout yourself in between, your choice is kept.\n\nNext: Android opens Modify system settings. Allow it for Sleep Timer Trial. You can turn it off there at any time.
Not active: accessibility access for Sleep Timer is off. Choose On again to allow it.
Screen turns off soon · then your screen timeout comes back
Locks the screen when a sleep timer ends.

Lets Sleep Timer lock the screen (and go to the Home screen first, if you choose) when a timer ends, and draw a dark layer if you turn on Goodnight. It does not read or record anything on your screen.

Turns on Do Not Disturb (your own priority settings, so alarms and the callers you allow still come through) until %1$s, and for at most 9 hours (so a daytime nap never silences your evening). Stopping the timer does not end it; end it early in the app or from the notification.
At start, lowers the media volume to %1$d %% (never raises it). After the pause your earlier volume comes back, unless you changed it during the timer.
Starts a timer at this time on the chosen days, unless one is already running. No extra permission.
Do Not Disturb access: turns on your Do Not Disturb when a timer starts, until the morning time you set (at most 9 hours).

When a timer starts, Sleep Timer turns on Do Not Disturb with its own rule called "Sleep timer". It uses your own priority settings, so your alarm still rings and the callers you allow still get through. It turns off at the morning time you choose (at most 9 hours after the start), or when you tap End Do Not Disturb.

Sleep Timer never reads your notifications and sends nothing anywhere.

Next: Android opens Do Not Disturb access (called Modes access on newer Android). Allow it for Sleep Timer Trial. You can turn it off there at any time.
Turned off: Do Not Disturb (Modes) access for Sleep Timer is off.
Not turned on: Do Not Disturb access was not allowed.
Not active: Do Not Disturb access for Sleep Timer is off. Choose On again to allow it.
Time for your sleep timer (%1$s) · tap to start
Stops your music, podcast or video after you fall asleep.
Could only mute — this player may keep playing
Dim the screen before the end
During the last minutes before the fade, the screen dims step by step. It never gets brighter, and your own brightness comes back as soon as the screen is off (or at once when you tap Stop).
Colours shift to a dark warm red while the screen dims.
After the pause, the screen goes almost black for a few seconds before it locks or turns off.
Choose Dark layer only if the screen ever looks brighter when the wind-down starts.
Needs the accessibility access used by Lock screen at end.
Now: lowers the screen brightness through its dark layer (no system setting is changed).
Now: dark layer only; the screen brightness is not touched.
Now: lowers the system brightness (Modify system settings); no warm tint or dark layer without the accessibility access.
Needs the accessibility access (Lock screen at end) or Modify system settings.
Not active: Goodnight needs the accessibility access or Modify system settings. Choose On again to allow it.

Goodnight lowers your screen brightness step by step before the timer ends. As soon as the screen is off, your own brightness and auto-brightness setting are put back. If you change the brightness yourself in between, your choice is kept.

With the accessibility access from Lock screen at end, Goodnight does not need this: it then dims through its own dark layer instead.

Next: Android opens Modify system settings. Allow it for Sleep Timer Trial. You can turn it off there at any time.
Turned off: Goodnight needs the accessibility access or Modify system settings, and neither is allowed now.
Not turned on: Goodnight needs Modify system settings or the accessibility access.
Screen turns off soon · then your brightness comes back
